verdict.rationale: Checkout.com's issuing docs state that it supports single-use virtual cards, which covers the core of the story. It also lets you set granular limits on transaction amounts, blocked industries and expiry, and apply your own accept/reject authorization rules. Locking a card to one specific merchant is not documented, since blocking industries is only category-level, and there is no developer-facing API detail. All evidence is marketing-level vendor copy with no hands-on corroboration. Missing for 10: an explicit single-merchant lock, an exact-amount (not just maximum) constraint, API docs for creating single-use cards programmatically, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a developer, I can issue single-use and tightly scoped cards — one purchase, one merchant, an exact amount — so a leaked number is worthless the moment it's used

citations.quote: Our platform supports physical cards and single or multi-use virtual cards for online, offline, or in-app payments.
Set granular limits like transaction amounts, blocked industries, and card expiry dates.
manage cardholders' spending limits, locations, and velocity
Automate transaction outcomes with accept or reject logic based on your own rules.
